Please come along to one of our open events for the Reception Class 2027-28 intake.
There’s no need to book, just come and join us for a tour of the school and to meet the Early Years Lead and the Head Teacher.
Tuesday 29 September at 10:30 am
Thursday 8 October at 5:30pm
Wednesday 11 November at 1:30pm
Friday 27 November at 10:00am
Head Teacher’s Welcome
St Michael’s is a Church of England Voluntary Aided Primary School for 4 to 11 year olds. We also provide for 3 and 4 year old pre-schoolers in the Catherine Wheel Nursery. We are a small school with one class in each year group. Our children come predominantly from Marston and also from other areas of Oxford.
Our aim is to serve our community by providing a high quality and wide-ranging education within the context of Christian belief and practice. We encourage an understanding of the meaning and significance of faith, celebrating the fact that our school includes families from many different cultures and faiths. We are committed to creating an environment in which every member of the school can thrive. Our school Christian values of Love, Determination, Responsibility, Respect, Kindness, Friendship and Honesty are the foundation on which we build our community and these guide our relationships with each other.
At St Michael’s we all work together to ensure that our school is a happy, calm and exciting place to learn. We are proud of our children’s very responsible, positive and caring attitudes to learning and school life. Our staff are dedicated to helping our children develop a lifelong love of learning so that they can fulfil their dreams and be the best that they can be.
In May 2025 we were subject to a Statutory Inspection of Methodist and Anglican Schools (SIAMS Inspection) – please read the inspection report to find out what the inspector thought about our school.
If you would like to see what our school looks like, please take the school tour.
Rosalind Owen
Head Teacher St Michael’s C of E Primary School

Governor Code of Conduct
All the governors of St Michael’s C of E Primary School agree to faithfully abide by this Code of Conduct.
We will abide by the Seven Nolan Principles of Public Life
Selflessness: We will act solely in terms of the public interest.
Integrity: We will avoid placing ourselves under any obligation to people or organisations that might try inappropriately to influence us in our work. We will not act or take decisions in order to gain financial or other material benefits for ourselves, our family, or our friends. We will declare and resolve any interests and relationships.
Objectivity: We will act and take decisions impartially, fairly and on merit, using the best evidence and without discrimination or bias.
Accountability: We are accountable to the public for our decisions and actions and will submit ourselves to the scrutiny necessary to ensure this.
Openness: We will act and take decisions in an open and transparent manner. Information will not be withheld from the public unless there are clear and lawful reasons for so doing.
Honesty: We will be truthful.
Leadership: We will exhibit these principles in our own behaviour. We will actively promote and robustly support the principles and be willing to challenge poor behaviour wherever it occurs.
We will focus on our core governance functions:

pageCache.text:
Christian Vision and Values
St Michael’s C of E Primary School is committed to creating an environment in which every member of the school community can thrive. Our school Christian values of Love, Determination, Responsibility, Respect, Kindness, Friendship and Honesty are the foundation on which we build our community, they guide our relationships with each other and express those things that enable us to flourish alongside each other. The most important of our values, and the one that binds them all together, is love.
The commandment to love is one of the most ancient to be found in the Bible.
In Deuteronomy it says: The Lord our God, the Lord is one. Love the Lord your God with all your heart and with all your soul and with all your strength. Deuteronomy 6:4-5
This was recast by Jesus: A new command I give you: Love one another. As I have loved you, so you must love one another. John 13:34
It is this principle of love that enables us to support and treat one another with kindness, respect, friendship and honesty and it is when we know we are loved that we can act with determination and responsibility.
As St Paul wrote in his first letter to the Corinthians: faith, hope and love abide. But the greatest of these is love. 1 Corinthians 13:13
St Michael’s Christian vision and values are the result of work undertaken by all members of the school community: our children, their families, our staff and our governors. In 2017, the children, staff and governors discussed, in their groups, which values were the most important to us. We also consulted with our children’s families, who told us the values that were most important to them. Though each group met separately, there was clear consensus and our seven values of Determination, Responsibility, Respect, Kindness, Friendship and Honesty, bound together by Love, have guided us ever since.

PTA – Enriching the educational experience of our children
St Michael’s PTA
The PTA Committee oversees the organisation of all the fundraising events that happen throughout the school year, including: Bonfire Night, Christmas and Easter Fairs, International Evening, School Disco, Football Tournaments, Summer Shindig, Summer Fair and the regular Film Club sessions.
Lots of parents and carers participate in the PTA in different ways: coming to our meetings, helping set up and clear up at events, running stalls, making cakes and crafts to sell, cooking burgers, serving tea and coffee and publicising events by making and displaying posters. Every contribution, whether it’s 10 minutes or 10 hours, is valuable. Over the past 3 years the PTA has raised over £20,000 for the school, funds that have been used to help pay for many additional things for school, including a class set of Chromebooks, and helping towards the cost of theatre visits, school trips, workshops and special visitors.
Everyone who takes part in the PTA has a positive impact on the children’s lives. As well being fun, it’s rewarding, it can be the foundation of many lasting friendships between parents across the school. You will get to make decisions about which events we hold, what happens at the events and how the money we raised is spent.
Please come and talk to a member of the PTA Committee if you would like to get involved.
